clue.text: Originally thinkers had to guess

parts.note: before any light of knowledge, early thinkers were groping blindly, so all they could offer was a random attempt at an answer

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a cryptic definition: thinkers in the days before enlightenment had nothing to go on, so every theory was a blind attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild attempt made with no real knowledge to guide it is the idiom for a guess.

clue.text: Successful bowler may get moving

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler who hits the wicket disturbs its upright posts

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bowls well is told to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the stumps are the three upright posts of the wicket, which a bowler aims to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to bestir oneself and start walking briskly.

clue.text: Put up with love — a repertory theatre …

definitions.note: drama set to music is a branch of theatre

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: put up in a down clue says the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: rep is short for repertory

explanation.surface: A company tolerates romance on its stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns A REP round to PERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a staged musical drama, a form of theatrical art.

clue.text: … might be so described, all things considered

definitions.meaning: a theatre with the audience on every side of the stage
taking everything into account, as in looked at in the whole

explanation.surface: A repertory theatre, viewed overall.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 2-down: a repertory theatre with seats all around its stage is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage encircled by seating is one sense; viewed overall, taking everything into account, is the other.

clue.text: Cut flat's rent — that's diplomatic

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: Slashing the rent on a flat would be a clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is the past participle of rend, torn, not a payment; it rearranges CUT and FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic person handles others with sensitivity and discretion.

clue.text: Add to the confusion in general

indicators.note: confusion in says the letters of the next word are muddled

explanation.surface: Muddy the waters further for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to increase its size by adding to it.

clue.text: The leaders in abandoned race could have finished

indicators.note: the leaders in says take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Had the frontrunners not quit, the race could have reached its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished' is in its sense of consummate, out-and-out, as in an arch rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means thoroughgoing or consummate, like a polished or accomplished villain.

clue.text: Recruiting officer supplying gear and food, accommodating an indefinite number

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

indicators.note: accommodating means housing one piece inside another

parts.note: cheer is an old word for food and drink, as in good cheer
n is the symbol for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A recruiter hands out equipment and rations to many new soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener's face appeared on the famous First World War recruiting poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener, British war minister, was the figure on the 'Your Country Needs You' enlistment poster.

clue.text: Author in French city died surrounded by birds

indicators.note: surrounded by says the city and the abbreviation sit inside the birds

parts.note: chickens are birds
Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: A writer in Provence died with poultry all around him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist wrote Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

clue.text: I have an adverse effect on one state, all the same

parts.note: to dent something is to damage or weaken it
one is the Roman numeral I
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A gloomy figure admits to harming an entire state, though it makes no difference to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Things all the same are exact matches of one another.

clue.text: Hidden drawback in contract

definitions.meaning: a snag concealed in a deal
to contract an illness is to pick it up

explanation.surface: There is a nasty clause buried in the deal's small print.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag lurking in an offer is the classic sense; to come down with a cold is the other.

clue.text: Speak of value …

parts.note: o' is a short form of 'of', as in o'clock
a rate is a valuation or price

explanation.surface: Talk about what something is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a speech, often pompously.

clue.text: … speak of fine food

indicators.note: speak of says the word for fine is to be said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: fine weather is fair weather

explanation.surface: Someone talks of excellent cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food served at a meal, as in good plain fare.

clue.text: Possibly 6 fish

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the other answer may be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6-down

explanation.surface: Perhaps six fish are swimming about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges ARCH, the answer to 6-down, into this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a cold-water fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Rabbit cheers almost everybody up

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: chin-chin is an informal toast meaning cheers

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A rabbit raises a toast to most of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CHINCHIN to CHINCHI; 'up' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of rabbit with soft grey fur is named after the South American rodent.

clue.text: Involve in return of ball caught in tree

indicators.note: return of says the whole assembled string is to be read backwards
caught in says one word is held inside the other

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A ball stuck in a tree, a nuisance to retrieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' looks as if it reverses only the ball, but it acts on the whole tree-with-ball unit, so the finished string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict or difficulty.

clue.text: Periods devoted to booze and marijuana, where vision is impaired

parts.note: a blind is slang for a drinking bout, so these are bouts of heavy drinking
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Binges on drink and drugs leave you seeing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in the field of view, or a subject someone cannot see clearly, is so named.

clue.text: 5 in ten chance the leaders get knocked out

definitions.note: 5 refers to the answer at 5-down, meaning make larger

indicators.note: the leaders get knocked out says the first letter of each of the two words is to be removed

explanation.surface: Odds of five in ten that the frontrunners will be eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T and C, the first letters of 'ten' and 'chance', leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost or augment something is to make it greater, the meaning of the 5-down answer.

clue.text: The spider and the fly

definitions.meaning: a spider is a creature that spins webs
in angling, a lure or artificial fly that revolves in the water

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme pairing of predator and prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that spins silk can be so called; anglers also use the word for a rotating lure or fly.

clue.text: Man who is practical about a roll

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth fellow is fussing over a bread bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who faces facts and acts sensibly rather than idealistically.

clue.text: Working, redoing what's overlooked

indicators.note: working in the sense of being worked over or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Busy reworking a task that someone had missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has been passed over or left unnoticed.

clue.text: I am over the hill, in a cul-de-sac

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
passé means past its best, out of date

explanation.surface: An ageing person confesses to being stuck in a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end, whether a street with no outlet or a deadlock in talks.

clue.text: Free party given by international organisation…

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: The United Nations throws a party at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' is a link putting the party after the organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or bond is to release or loosen it.

clue.text: . a party that's theatrical

definitions.meaning: a faction or side in politics

explanation.surface: A political group known for its flamboyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction holding shared views is one sense; ostentatiously affected behaviour is the other.

clue.text: "Gönerdämmerung" features in such a vocabulary

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Wagnerian title appears in some lexicon.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed word is a mangled Götterdämmerung, the twilight of the gods, a byword for apocalyptic destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Götterdämmerung, the collapse of the gods' world, stands for total chaos and devastation.

clue.text: Opposed to a road being put up for sale

parts.note: v stands for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: being put up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lane is a minor road

explanation.surface: Objecting to a street going on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put up' turns LANE to ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means corruptly open to bribery, so one's services can be bought.

clue.text: Fog makes you puff, short of breath initially

indicators.note: short of says something is removed from the end of the word

parts.note: a puff is a promotional write-up, such as cover copy on a book

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: Getting out of breath, you puff in the mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' and 'initially' remove B, the first letter of 'breath', from the end of BLURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To fog is to make indistinct or smudge, as fog obscures outlines.

clue.text: Young man, one who is under instruction?

definitions.meaning: in Scots and Roman law, a minor in the care of a guardian
a learner at school or with a teacher

explanation.surface: A youth who is still being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the word means a child ward below puberty; generally it means a schoolchild or student.

clue.text: Sock — good one missing cheek

parts.note: a sock can mean the inner sole placed inside a shoe

indicators.note: missing says one word goes without the other

parts.note: nice is a mild word for good
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A punch, a decent one gone astray, and a slap on the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes I from NICE, leaving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is impudent rudeness, the same as disrespectful boldness.

clue.text: Spiritualists used to alter circumstances completely

definitions.meaning: Victorian seances featured table-turning, where furniture supposedly moved
an idiom for reversing one's position relative to an opponent

explanation.surface: Victorian mediums once changed everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse a situation so the losing side now has the advantage.
